skill.name: beat-sync-editing
skill.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "cut to the beat", "fix the pacing", "edit this sequence", "sync cuts to music/BPM", "add a match cut / J-cut / L-cut", "build a speed ramp", or "plan a shot sequence / edit timeline". Covers editing rhythm, transitions, retiming, and translating an edit plan to an NLE or a code timeline (Remotion/AE frames).
skill.summary: Plan video cuts, audio transitions, and speed changes around musical phrases.
skill.author: iart-ai

content.value_statement: Cuts that ignore musical phrases can feel out of sync even at the right tempo. Build a frame-based edit plan from the tempo, first-beat offset, and key musical moments.
actual_capabilities: Convert tempo, frame rate, and the first-beat offset into frame positions for cuts and accents.
Plan shot lengths across the opening, buildup, climax, and resolution.
Recommend cuts on action, visual match cuts, and J-cuts or L-cuts with frame offsets.
Specify speed ramp keyframes that place the slowest moment on a chosen beat.
Map edit timing to a video editor, Remotion, or After Effects.
limitations: The skill provides edit plans and timing examples, not automatic media edits or rendered videos.
It explains offline tempo detection but does not include an audio analysis tool.
A single tempo grid may drift on tracks with tempo changes. Verify against actual beat positions.
Slow motion quality depends on the footage and the interpolation available in your editor.

use_cases.title: Time a Short Product Video
use_cases.description: Use musical phrases for shot changes and place the main product reveal on the drop.

use_cases.title: Smooth a Dialogue Scene Change
use_cases.description: Choose a J-cut or L-cut and specify exactly where the audio changes relative to the picture cut.

use_cases.title: Transfer an Edit Plan to Remotion
use_cases.description: Convert a shot list into start frames, clip durations, audio offsets, and retiming notes.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Cut Frames
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Create a timing grid from a known tempo.
prompt_templates.prompt: My track is [BPM] at [fps], and its first beat is at [seconds]. List the frames for the first [count] four-beat phrase starts.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Audio Transition
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Connect two shots without cutting picture and sound at the same frame.
prompt_templates.prompt: Shot A ends with [outgoing sound], and shot B starts with [incoming sound]. Recommend a J-cut or L-cut at frame [frame] and specify the audio offset.

prompt_templates.title: Shape a Sequence Around the Drop
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Vary shot lengths and emphasize one visual moment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a [duration]-second edit at [fps] using [BPM], [first-beat offset], and [drop time]. Use [shot list] to plan the opening, buildup, climax, and resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Frame-Based Timeline Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Specify timing for a Remotion or After Effects timeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate [edit plan] to a [Remotion or After Effects] timing sheet at [fps]. Include clip starts, durations, transition overlaps, and audio offsets. Specify speed ramp keyframes and verify the impact against [beat timestamps].

output_examples.input: Give me four phrase starts at 120 BPM and 30 fps. The first beat is 0.2 seconds into the track.
output_examples.output: Place the four-beat phrase starts at frames 6, 66, 126, and 186. The first-beat offset shifts the entire grid by six frames.

output_examples.input: The next speaker should be heard before the picture cuts at frame 180. Start their audio eight frames early.
output_examples.output: Use a J-cut. Start the next speaker at frame 172 and keep the outgoing picture visible until frame 180.

output_examples.input: Plan a speed ramp at 30 fps for a product reveal on frame 150.
output: Play at normal speed through frame 142.
Ease down to 25 percent speed at frame 150, where the reveal lands on the beat.
Ease back to normal speed by frame 162 and check the slow section for interpolation artifacts.

best_practices: Measure where the first beat lands instead of assuming it starts at time zero.
Round each cumulative beat position to the nearest frame to avoid accumulating timing errors.
Use phrase boundaries for major cuts and reserve the strongest visual for the musical drop.
anti_patterns: Cutting on every beat regardless of the desired pacing.
Using a dissolve to compensate for a poorly placed cut.
Keeping every shot the same length through the buildup and climax.

faq.question: What information do I need to start?
faq.answer: Provide the tempo in beats per minute, timeline frame rate, and first-beat offset. For a full edit plan, add your shot list and key music timestamps.

faq.question: Can the skill detect tempo from my audio?
faq.answer: It describes offline detection and tap tempo but does not include an audio analyzer. Bring the measured tempo and first-beat offset to the planning step.

faq.question: How do I prevent timing drift?
faq.answer: Round each absolute beat position instead of rounding the interval between beats. Compare the result with the track, especially if the tempo changes.

faq.question: How do J-cuts and L-cuts differ?
faq.answer: In a J-cut, incoming audio begins before the picture changes. In an L-cut, outgoing audio continues after the picture changes.

faq.question: Can I use the plan in my editor?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the frame positions in a video editor, Remotion, or After Effects. Apply the plan to your project manually.

faq.question: Where should a speed ramp reach its slowest point?
faq.answer: Align the slowest moment with the beat you want to emphasize. Preview the result and check whether frame blending or optical flow improves the motion.
